human-information-processing.title: Chapter 3: Human Computer Interaction
human-information-processing.summary: Human Information Processing (HIP) studies how people receive, process, and respond to information.

sections.heading: HUMAN INFORMATION PROCESSING
paragraphs: Human Information Processing (HIP) studies how people receive, process, and respond to information. It connects psychology (how the brain works) and computer science (how machines process data).
list: Goal: Make technology easier, faster, and safer to use.
Human factors = understanding what people can and cannot do well.
Limitations: memory lapses, slower reaction under stress.
Purpose: create systems that match human abilities.

sections.heading: TASK MODELING & PROBLEM-SOLVING MODEL
list: Task Modeling = step-by-step breakdown of how a user completes a task.

sections.heading: HUMAN REACTION
list: Focuses on how fast and accurate humans can respond.

sections.heading: IMPORTANCE IN HCI
list: Better interface design = improved user experience.

sections.heading: SUMMARY:
list: HIP = study of how humans handle information.
Human-factors knowledge helps create user-friendly systems.
Application: Better apps, websites, and systems.

sensation-and-perception-in-hci.title: Chapter 4: Human Computer Interaction
sensation-and-perception-in-hci.summary: Sensation and perception govern how users receive and interpret information from a system.

sections.heading: SENSATION AND PERCEPTION OF INFORMATION
paragraphs: Sensation: The process of detecting physical stimuli through the senses.
Perception: The process of interpreting and making sense of the sensation.
Key Idea: Sensation = input, Perception = meaning.
Users rely on senses to receive information from a system.
Perception helps them understand and act correctly.

sections.heading: VISUAL PERCEPTION
paragraphs: The most dominant sense in HCI.
list: Icons grouped together are seen as related.

sections.heading: AUDITORY PERCEPTION
paragraphs: Hearing used for alerts, notifications, voice interaction.
list: Key aspects:Volume – must be noticeable but not irritating.
Recognition of patterns – familiar sounds are easier to identify.

sections.heading: Haptic (Touch) Perception
paragraphs: Users also process information through touch.

sections.heading: Limits of Sensory Perception
paragraphs: Design Tip: Keep interfaces simple, clear, and accessible.
list: Visual overload – too much info on screen = confusion.
Auditory overload – too many notifications = irritation.
Individual differences – color blindness, hearing loss, or disability.

sections.heading: SUMMARY
paragraphs: Good design = information that is easy to sense and understand.
list: In HCI, designers must consider:Vision (colors, shapes, grouping)
